E1-C01.claim: J.P. Morgan's 12-month time-series momentum across four asset classes had a backtest Sharpe of 1.21.
E1-C01.evidence: All-asset Sharpe 1.21 (1992-2014); cross-sectional 0.44; enhanced 0.82; EMV 0.78 (1972-2014). IS; 10 bp one-way assumed; net/gross unlabelled.
E1-C01.implication: CONTEXT/DROP as an alpha prior: 1.21 is an IS ceiling. Live prior 0.3-0.4 diversified.

E1-C02.evidence: 12m Sharpe equity 0.82 / bonds 0.75 / commodities 0.63 vs 1m 0.33 / 0.27 / 0.19. IS, 1992-2014.
E1-C02.implication: BUILD (design rule): trend and sizing cards use 6-12m windows. Never 1m trend.

E1-C03.claim: Cash yield was a large share of historical CTA returns.
E1-C03.evidence: After-fee CTA return 7.4%/yr in 1994-2010, of which 4.1 points cash; -1.9%/yr in 2011-13. Live, net, 4-index average.
E1-C03.implication: BUILD (accounting rule): all cards report excess-of-cash returns; flat periods earn T-bill.

E1-C04.claim: AQR attributes 2010s trend weakness to fewer large moves, not decay.
E1-C04.evidence: Qualitative attribution; no numbers on the page.
E1-C04.implication: BACKLOG: re-test B3 after 126 more OOS sessions. Do not loosen the gate.

E1-C05.claim: A live diversified managed-futures fund earned about 3%/yr over cash net of fees over 10 years.
E1-C05.evidence: AQMIX 10y 5.44% vs T-bill 2.42%; 5y 15.04% vs 3.70%; since Jan-2010 4.54% vs 1.48%; as of 30-Sep-2026. Live, net.
E1-C05.implication: PRIOR: diversified trend excess about 3%/yr net (Sharpe about 0.3 if 10% vol; vol unverified).

E1-C06.claim: S&P 500 long/flat trend beat buy-and-hold in the J.P. Morgan sample window but not after publication.
E1-C06.evidence: 12m rule R/V 1.32 vs 0.81 (1992-2014); 1.02 vs 1.16 (2015-Sep 2026); return 10.9% vs 13.8%; max DD -18.9% vs -19.3%. Gross, no cash; Shiller monthly averages.
E1-C06.implication: DROP as alpha. CONTEXT as a drawdown overlay ≤1.0 (macro rule). DC3.

E1-C07.claim: J.P. Morgan AM's forward-P/E chart explains little 1-year return, and its 5-year R² decayed.
E1-C07.evidence: 1y R² 8% (Sep-2020 ed.), 7% (Mar-2024), 5% (Mar-2026); 5y 44% → 29% → 28%. IS, overlapping monthly, US.
E1-C07.implication: DROP for 1y timing. CONTEXT for 5-10y return-expectation display with wide bands.

E1-C08.claim: CAPE ranks long-horizon returns but its level failed OOS after 1990.
E1-C08.evidence: Full-history R² 0.05 / 0.16 / 0.29 (1y/5y/10y); post-1990 10y 0.86 IS; OOS R² -0.54 (10y) with correlation +0.93; Jun-2013 forecast 2.9%/yr real vs 9.5% realized.
E1-C08.implication: CONTEXT. Any valuation overlay must use expanding-window percentiles, not regression levels. DC1, DC2.

E1-C09.claim: BofA says normalized P/E explains about 80% of 10-year returns but little over 1 year.

E1-C10.claim: BofA's Sell Side Indicator is a contrarian sentiment gauge.
E1-C10.evidence: Strategists' average equity allocation since 1980; 43% in 2012 = buy; "more effective since GFC" (no stats given).
E1-C10.implication: BACKLOG: proprietary, cannot replicate. Korean analogue (investor-type flow extremes) via DC5.

E1-C11.claim: CAPE above 30 has not been a reliable 1-year sell signal.
E1-C11.evidence: 102 months (through Sep-2023): mean fwd 1y price +3.0%, 58% positive vs 6.7% / 65% unconditional; S&P +208% from Sep-2017 (first >30) to Sep-2026. Price-only.
E1-C11.implication: DROP as a timing card. At most a [0.5, 1.0] multiplier if DC2 passes the gate.

E1-C12.claim: Hedge fund crowding hit a record without immediate payback.
E1-C12.evidence: Nov-2023: 70% of longs in top-10 (22-year high); VIP +31% vs S&P +19% YTD; 735 funds, $2.4tn.
E1-C12.implication: CONTEXT: crowding is a risk monitor, never a direction signal.

E1-C13.claim: Momentum/crowding unwinds hit systematic funds in 2025-2026.
E1-C13.evidence: Jan-2026: GS systematic long/short about -1% in 10 days; UBS US quant -2.8%. Jul-2026: momentum -3%+ for 2 weeks; GS systematic -2.1% / -3.1%; weakest since Dec-2023; momentum at highest level since 2002 just before.
E1-C13.implication: BUILD: volatility scaling + bear gate on momentum (already decided). Add a factor-vol trigger (DC5).

E1-C14.claim: The Jun-Jul 2026 unwind cost long-only momentum 16 points relative in five weeks.
E1-C14.evidence: MTUM -18.0% vs SPY -2.0% (22-Jun to 29-Jul-2026); SPHB -14.1%; USMV +4.3%. Price-only.
E1-C14.implication: BUILD: the momentum card must report worst-5-week relative loss. Test a crash gate on KRX (DC4, DC8).

E1-C15.claim: US momentum has a positive long-run premium, weaker in large caps after discovery, and hedges value.
E1-C15.evidence: UMD 8.3%/yr, Sharpe 0.50 (1927-2013); large-cap Sharpe 0.24 (1991-2013, OOS); correlation with HML -0.4. Gross.
E1-C15.implication: PRIOR: large-cap long/short momentum Sharpe 0.25 gross before haircuts. Always pair with value (C17).

E1-C16.claim: Dynamic (volatility- and state-aware) momentum roughly quadruples the static Sharpe.
E1-C16.evidence: Dynamic Sharpe 1.18 vs about 0.3 static (1927-2013, IS); crashes Jul-Aug 1932 (losers +232%) and Mar-May 2009 (losers +163%).
E1-C16.implication: BUILD (already decided): sigma126 scaling, 12% target, cap 1.0, bear gate floor 0.5.

E1-C17.claim: Multi-measure, industry-neutral, current-price value beats book-to-price.
E1-C17.evidence: Sharpe 0.26 vs 0.07 since 1990; correlation 0.9; naive value only 32% within-industry risk; impact 17 bp at 2% ADV / 28 bp at 6%; timing needs >0.1 Sharpe skill, tilts ±12%. IS, gross.
E1-C17.implication: BUILD-candidate (KRX via OpenDART PIT): B/P + E/P + CF/P + S/P, industry-neutral. No factor timing.

E1-C18.claim: AQR said in May-2020 that extreme value spreads made the medium-term odds favour value.
E1-C18.evidence: Spread at 100th percentile; HML worst quarter since 1963 (1Q2020). After: VLUE +3.4 pts/yr vs IVV (Jul-2021 to Jun-2026) but -12.0 (2023) and -17.8 (2024); spreads back at tech-bubble highs in Aug-2022.
E1-C18.implication: CONTEXT: show the value spread as an expected-return gauge. Never size up above 1.0.

E1-C19.claim: Research Affiliates (2016) said recent factor returns were inflated by valuation changes, warning low volatility and profitability were expensive.
E1-C19.evidence: Low vol: >100% of return from valuation expansion, 0.82%/yr adjusted; profitability 0.39%/yr adjusted; value cheapest decile (1967-2015Q3). After: USMV -5.9 pts/yr and QUAL -1.0 pts/yr vs IVV over 10y; VLUE -3.5 pts/yr in the first 5 years.
E1-C19.implication: BUILD (reporting): model cards show valuation-adjusted factor returns next to raw returns.

E1-C20.claim: Long-only MSCI factor ETFs did not reliably beat the S&P 500 after 2016.
E1-C20.evidence: 10y to Jun-2026 excess vs IVV: MTUM +2.1, QUAL -1.0, VLUE -0.0, USMV -5.9 pts/yr; cum 2021-2025 +64 / +82 / +80 / +50% vs IVV +96%. Live, net.
E1-C20.implication: DROP factor-ETF rotation. PRIOR: long-only factor tilt active return ≈ 0 ± 2%/yr.

E1-C21.claim: Rules-based factor indices can drift into concentrated bets.
E1-C21.implication: BUILD: single-name cap (e.g., 5%) and sector bands; publish factor-purity and concentration in every card. Korea: Samsung/SK hynix caps (macro).

E1-C22.claim: Most professional active equity funds lag their index after fees.
E1-C22.evidence: US large-cap: 78.78% (2025), 85.59% (10y), 92.89% (20y); 20y survival 34.61%. Europe equity 10y 97.02%. Japan large-cap 10y 83% (49% in 2025). Live, net.
E1-C22.implication: CONTEXT: base rate for gate step 5; supports keeping the p ≤ 0.10 benchmark test.

E1-C23.claim: J.P. Morgan (2017) said alternative data mostly carries small Sharpe ratios and high-Sharpe datasets decay.
E1-C23.evidence: Most datasets carry only a small positive Sharpe (paraphrase); Twitter example IR 1.4 after 5 bp since 2013 (vendor, short sample). After: AIEQ 5y 4.18% vs SPY 12.65% (to Aug-2026).
E1-C23.implication: DROP for now. Revisit only after linear cards pass.

E1-C24.claim: ML gains in academic tests concentrate in hard-to-arbitrage stocks and shrink after costs.
E1-C24.evidence: Machine learning up to doubles regression-strategy performance (gross, US); profits shrink excluding microcaps, distressed stocks and high-vol periods, and with costs.
E1-C24.implication: BACKLOG: only with liquidity filters and 2x costs.

E1-C25.claim: Published anomalies shrink out of sample and after publication; many fail with microcaps controlled.
E1-C25.evidence: 64% of 447 anomalies insignificant with NYSE breakpoints/VW (85% at t>3); JKP: most replicate in 93 countries; McLean-Pontiff SSRN version: about 15% OOS and about 50% post-publication decay.
E1-C25.implication: PRIOR: keep the 60% live haircut (gate step 9); avoid liquidity-type anomalies.

E1-C26.claim: High-turnover anomalies rarely survive costs; buy/hold bands are the best fix.
E1-C26.evidence: Strategies with >50% monthly turnover generally insignificant after costs (US).
E1-C26.implication: BUILD: hysteresis/buy-hold bands on every stock-level card; report turnover.

E1-C27.claim: Volatility targeting improves Sharpe for equities and credit, not bonds, FX or commodities, and trims left tails.
E1-C27.evidence: 60+ assets, daily since 1926 (Man Group, JPM 2018), IS.
E1-C27.implication: CONTEXT: keep the macro decision (momentum sleeves). Flag the partial conflict; no up-weighting above 1.0.

E1-C28.claim: Hedge fund alpha and quant demand were at records just before the 2026 unwinds.
E1-C28.evidence: GS: HF return 11.8% (2025), alpha highest in 30+ years, $79bn inflows, quant demand outstripping supply (12-Feb-2026); Jul-2026 quant drawdown followed.
E1-C28.implication: CONTEXT: a capacity/crowding risk flag in the momentum card. No timing rule.

E2-C01.claim: The US market's first half-hour return predicts its last half-hour return.
E2-C01.evidence: SPY 1993-2013: R² 1.6% IS / 1.4% OOS; timing strategy 6.67%/yr, Sharpe 1.08 gross; 4.46%/yr after spread; FOMC-day R² 11%.
E2-C01.implication: DROP: break-even ≈1.3 bp per side vs 50 bp (US) / 35 bp (KRX).

E2-C02.claim: Korean market intraday momentum is weak.
E2-C02.evidence: KOSEF 200 ETF, Apr 2008-Apr 2021: coefficient 2.06 (p 0.084); R² 1.9% IS / 0.9% OOS.

E2-C03.claim: Intraday momentum is driven by short-gamma hedging and leveraged-ETF flows, and reverses over the next days.
E2-C03.evidence: 60+ futures 1974-2020; stock-level short gamma raises momentum ~68%, gamma-theta range breaches ~91%.
E2-C03.implication: CONTEXT: don't chase flow-driven closes; expect partial reversal.

E2-C04.claim: US stocks show a cross-sectional end-of-day reversal worth only a few bp.
E2-C04.evidence: 1993-2019: VW 3.45 bp/day (8.7%/yr), EW 4.45 bp/day, gross; stable over time.
E2-C04.implication: DROP: needs intraday execution at bp-level cost.

E2-C05.claim: Half-hour return periodicity is real but not profitable after spreads.
E2-C05.evidence: NYSE 2001-2005: 3.01 bp same half-hour next day, significant up to 40 days; not profitable net.

E2-C06.claim: US momentum is earned overnight, while value, profitability, investment and size premia are earned intraday.
E2-C06.evidence: US 1993-2013 excluding microcaps: momentum 0.98%/month overnight (t 3.84) vs −0.02% intraday; ROE −0.95% overnight vs +1.42% intraday.
E2-C06.implication: BUILD-design: fill momentum cards in the closing auction; test on KRX (DC-E2-01).

E2-C07.claim: The overnight drift in E-mini futures disappears after spreads, except a conditional buy-the-dip version.
E2-C07.evidence: ES 1998-2020: 2-3 a.m. ET 3.7% annualized (1.48 bp/day); Sharpe 1.1 gross → −0.5 net; conditional version 1.1 net.
E2-C07.implication: DROP (no 2 a.m. execution); CONTEXT: selloffs into the close revert overnight.

E2-C08.implication: DROP as a strategy; CONTEXT for DC-E2-12.

E2-C09.claim: The QQQ 5-minute ORB's headline result does not survive realistic slippage.
E2-C09.evidence: Paper: 1,484% 2016-2023, 33% alpha net of commissions. Replication: break-even ~2.2¢/share; Sharpe 0.23 at 2¢; 76% of filtered P&L in 2022; bootstrap CI overlaps QQQ.

E2-C10.claim: ORB on "stocks in play" reports Sharpe 2.81 only under no-slippage, 4x-leverage assumptions.
E2-C10.evidence: US 2016-2023: top-20 Sharpe 2.81, 1,637%; full universe Sharpe 0.48; $0.0035/share commission, no slippage, stops at 10% ATR.

E2-C11.claim: ORB's gross signal (~0.13R) is eaten by CFD spreads across five index markets.
E2-C11.evidence: NQ, SPX, Dow, DAX, FTSE CFDs, Jan 2015-Jun 2026: net NQ +0.002R, four markets negative.

E2-C12.claim: Price impact scales with the square root of order size relative to volume.
E2-C12.evidence: Impact ≈ Yσ√(Q/V), Y ~1, for Q/V from 10⁻⁴ to a few %; TSE 8 years: exponent 0.5 ± 0.1; 8m US institutional trades: linear-to-square-root crossover.
E2-C12.implication: BUILD (cost model): impact term plus a 1% of ADV cap on every card.

E2-C13.claim: Institutional costs are far below academic estimates, yet short-term reversal still fails at reasonable size.
E2-C13.evidence: $1.7tn, 21 markets, 19 years: costs about 10x below prior estimates; ~$1tn, 19 markets, 1998-2011: reversal does not survive.
E2-C13.implication: CONTEXT: retail costs (35-50 bp) are far above institutional, so never import gross academic results for high-turnover cards.

E2-C14.claim: Strategies with one-sided monthly turnover above ~50% rarely survive costs; one-month reversal turns strongly negative net.
E2-C14.evidence: US 1963-2012: reversal turnover 90.87%/month; gross 0.37%/month (t 1.71), net −1.28%/month (t −6.02); with buy/hold band −0.72%/month.
E2-C14.implication: BUILD (gate rule): turnover ≤50%/month target plus break-even screen; Korean reversal goes to BACKLOG until DC-E2-02/03 pass.

E2-C15.claim: Reversal returns are pay for providing liquidity and peak when the VIX is high.
E2-C15.evidence: Reversal expected returns and Sharpe rose sharply in 2007-09; predictable with VIX.
E2-C15.implication: BACKLOG: VIX-conditioned weekly reversal (DC-E2-09); keep the 1.0x hold.

E2-C16.claim: Closing auctions are the deepest liquidity event of the US day and keep growing.
E2-C16.evidence: 3.1% (2010) → 7.5% (2018) of volume; ~9-9.44% of consolidated notional (2024); NYSE-listed 10.5-14.2% depending on source and measure; >34% on Russell day 2024; NYSE Q1 2026 605.5m shares/day, record 3.57bn on 20 Mar 2026.
E2-C16.implication: BUILD (execution convention): closing-auction fill as default for daily-close cards.

E2-C17.claim: Closing prices carry transient auction pressure that reverses overnight.
E2-C17.evidence: US: average absolute deviation 8.1 bp; >63 bp in 1% of cases; almost complete overnight reversal.
E2-C17.implication: BUILD (test rule): skip-day and t+1 fill variants for every reversal card (DC-E2-03, DC-E2-11).

E2-C18.claim: Support/resistance has an order-placement basis, but the measured effect on intraday trend interruptions is small.
E2-C18.evidence: FX Jan 1996-Mar 1998: published levels 60.8% vs arbitrary 56.2%; lasts ≥5 days; 70% of levels end in 0, 96% in 0 or 5. Stops cluster beyond round numbers, take-profits at them; stop cascades.
E2-C18.implication: CONTEXT: avoid round-number stop placement; no S/R entry card.

E2-C19.claim: US retail liquidity demanders systematically lose around round numbers.
E2-C19.evidence: >100m trades: over-buying one penny below and over-selling one penny above round numbers; losses close to $1bn/yr.
E2-C19.implication: BACKLOG data-check on KRX (DC-E2-05); never simulate fills at round numbers on touch.

E2-C20.claim: Stop orders fill far from the stop in fast markets.
E2-C20.evidence: Stops become market orders. 6 May 2010: >20,000 trades >60% away. 24 Aug 2015: SPY open −5.2%, IVV −20%+, JPM −13.3% in 65 s.
E2-C20.implication: BUILD (fill rule): stops fill at the next available price; no fill while limit-locked (DC-E2-08).

E2-C21.claim: Fewer than 1% of day traders are reliably profitable after fees, and aggregate day trading loses every year.
E2-C21.evidence: Taiwan 1992-2006: bottom-ranked traders 11.5 bp/day gross → −28.9 net; net negative in all 15 years; >75% quit within 2 years. Taiwan 1995-1999: individuals lose 3.8 points/yr, mainly via taxes (34%) and commissions (32%).
E2-C21.implication: CONTEXT: base rate; no intraday-trading UI nudges.

E2-C22.claim: Day trading for a living is virtually impossible in Brazil.
E2-C22.evidence: Index futures 2013-2015: 97% of 300+ day persisters lost; 1.1% earned above minimum wage.

E2-C23.claim: Korea's 2020 retail boom showed very high turnover, mostly intraday trading, and negative net returns for new investors.
E2-C23.evidence: 204,004 accounts, Mar-Oct 2020: new investors net −1.2% vs existing +15.0%; 55.4% of trading intraday; costs −4.0 points; turnover ~1,600%/yr; 46% of all investors lost.
E2-C23.implication: CONTEXT: QUANTGEN's audience base rate argues against intraday features.

E2-C24.claim: Robinhood-era retail evidence is mixed, and retail execution costs vary widely.
E2-C24.evidence: Herding stocks −4.7% 20-day abnormal return; crowd portfolio did well 2018-2020; round-trip execution −0.07% to −0.46% excluding commissions.
E2-C24.implication: CONTEXT: 50 bp per side for US via KIS is a plausible conservative stress.

E2-C25.claim: KRX VI, limit and auction rules interrupt intraday technical mechanics.
E2-C25.evidence: Dynamic VI 3%/6% (2%/4% in the closing auction), static 10%, 2-minute call; ±30% limit since 15 Jun 2015; closing call 15:20-15:30 with random end ≤30 s; overheating triggers a 3-day periodic call.
E2-C25.implication: BUILD (data hygiene): unfillable-day flags; regime flags at 2015.

E2-C26.claim: KRX's coarse ticks plus the 0.20% sell tax set a round-trip floor of about 25-45 bp before commission and impact.
E2-C26.implication: BUILD (cost model): tick-band spread floor; 35 bp per side adequate for liquid names only (DC-E2-06).

E2-C27.claim: Nextrade extends Korean trading to 12 hours with cheaper fees, but its stock list and share are unstable.
E2-C27.evidence: Launched Mar 2025; sessions 08:00-08:50 / 09:00:30-15:20 / 15:40-20:00; fees 20-40% lower; 15% cap; stocks 800→630 (2025)→610 (Q3 2026); value ratio vs KRX 26.9%→49.4%→~21%; share 10.64%→9.10% after KRX after-hours launch.
E2-C27.implication: BUILD (data hygiene): KRX official close only; verify the KIS close source (DC-E2-10).

E2-C28.claim: The US half-penny tick (Nov 2025) lowers spread costs for tick-constrained names but doesn't change retail broker costs.
E2-C28.evidence: SEC 18 Sep 2024: $0.005 tick for qualifying stocks ≥$1; access fee cap $0.001; compliance Nov 2025.
E2-C28.implication: CONTEXT: regime flag for US cards after Nov 2025.

E2-C29.claim: Classic US intraday predictors may have decayed after publication.
E2-C29.evidence: SPY/QQQ 2007-2018: intraday momentum and overnight effects diminished; conflicts with futures evidence through 2020.
E2-C29.implication: CONTEXT: apply the 60% haircut; another reason to drop.

E2-C30.claim: Every short-horizon card should report a break-even per-side cost and be rejected before the gate if it is below 2x the pre-registered cost.
E2-C30.evidence: Break-even = gross annual return / (2 × annual turnover). Examples: SPY intraday momentum ≈1.3 bp, overnight drift ≈0.7 bp, QQQ ORB ≈0.5-2 bp, against 35-50 bp.
E2-C30.implication: BUILD (card header field plus pre-gate screen).

E3-C01.claim: Diversified TSMOM has a 130-year simulated record with a net Sharpe of about 0.77.
E3-C01.evidence: 67 markets, 1/3/12-month signals, 10% vol, 2/20 fees plus period costs; 1880–2013 gross 14.9%, net 11.2%, vol 9.7%; 2000–13 net Sharpe 0.62; correlation with equities 0.00.
E3-C01.implication: CONTEXT: a prior for a 50+-market book only.

E3-C02.claim: In 1985–2009 every one of 58 liquid futures showed positive 12-month TSMOM.
E3-C02.evidence: 52/58 significant; diversified gross Sharpe above 1; alpha 1.58%/month (t 7.99); smile coefficient 1.99 (t 3.88); in-sample, gross.

E3-C03.claim: Single-asset trend is weak; diversified Sharpe is a breadth effect.
E3-C03.evidence: Median single-asset gross Sharpe 0.34–0.39 vs 1.17 (58 traditional assets), 1.34 (82 alternative, incl. KOSPI 200) and 1.60 (all 156); 1985–2017; gross.
E3-C03.implication: BUILD: single-index trend cards must not claim alpha; correct the prior to ≈ 0.3–0.4 gross per asset.

E3-C04.evidence: 8/55 assets significant at 10%; out-of-sample R² < 0 for 45/55; pooled t 4.34 < bootstrap critical values 4.83 (pairs) and 12.53 (wild); TSH ≈ TSMOM (p 0.19); unscaled t 1.68; 1985–2015.
E3-C04.implication: CONTEXT: require portfolio-level claims; print TSH and vol-scaled controls.

E3-C05.claim: Volatility scaling drives much of TSMOM's measured alpha.
E3-C05.evidence: Monthly alpha: scaled TSMOM 1.08%, unscaled TSMOM 0.39%, unscaled buy-and-hold 0.40%, scaled buy-and-hold 0.73%; 55 futures, 1985–2009; gross.
E3-C05.implication: BUILD: every trend card prints a vol-scaled long-only control at the same exposure.

E3-C06.claim: Moving-average crossovers and TSMOM are one family.
E3-C06.evidence: R² > 80% in all regressions; TSMOM(260d) Sharpe 1.45, MACROSS(32,128) 1.33, TSMOM(22d) 0.97; 58 instruments, 1985–2015; gross.
E3-C06.implication: BUILD: count MA, Donchian and TSMOM variants as trials of one family (DSR).

E3-C07.claim: Better volatility estimators and continuous signals cut turnover by about 36% at no Sharpe cost.
E3-C07.evidence: Yang–Zhang −17%, TREND −24%, both −36%; costs 163 → 105 bp/yr; Sharpe 1.15 vs 1.11; 56 futures, 1983–2013.
E3-C07.implication: BUILD: vote-share or continuous signal plus a band; range volatility where OHLC exists.

E3-C08.claim: The 2009–2013 trend drought appears in both academic and industry data.
E3-C08.evidence: TSMOM Sharpe 0.01 gross / −0.09 net (BK); SG Trend −1.8% cumulative 2009–13 (Man); correlations elevated from late 2008 to mid-2014 (HOP 2017).
E3-C08.implication: CONTEXT: B3's "no edge after 2009" replicates the industry.

E3-C09.claim: Net CTA returns split sharply around 2009.
E3-C09.evidence: Barclay Systematic CAGR 6.98% in 2000–08 (9/9 years positive) vs −0.30% in 2009–18 (3/10); 2009–25 mean/SD 0.30 with 9/17 years positive.
E3-C09.implication: CONTEXT: step 8's 60% rule would reject the net industry index over 2009–25.

E3-C10.claim: 2022 was the best year in SG index history.
E3-C10.evidence: SG CTA +20.1% (best since 2000), SG Trend +27.3%, STTI +11.3%; 27/30 programs positive; trend followers +11% to +40%.
E3-C10.implication: CONTEXT: trend pays in slow inflation and rates bear markets.

E3-C11.claim: 2023–2025 were lean years well below equities.

E3-C12.claim: April 2025 produced the worst rolling 12-month loss in SG Trend history.
E3-C12.evidence: −18.6% to 30 Apr 2025 (prior worst −16.0%, Jan 2019); −9.3% year-to-date to 13 Apr; April −4.9%; 30% best-to-worst spread.
E3-C12.implication: CONTEXT: pre-register a −20% drawdown expectation (≈ 80% chance in 25 years at Sharpe 0.5).

E3-C13.claim: 2026 has been a strong trend year so far.
E3-C13.evidence: SG Trend +15.85% and SG CTA +15.67% year-to-date (estimates, 1 Oct 2026); to August, SG Trend +11.07% vs S&P 500 TR +13.14%.
E3-C13.implication: CONTEXT: do not tune on 2026; treat it as forward record.

E3-C14.claim: "Trend" is a wide distribution of manager outcomes.
E3-C14.evidence: 2024: average pairwise correlation 0.78 yet about a 15% range; 2022: +11% to +40%; cross-sectional SD ≈ 2%/month, stable 2010–24.
E3-C14.implication: CONTEXT: one QUANTGEN configuration ≈ one manager draw; use an ensemble.

E3-C15.claim: Managed-futures returns are largely TSMOM, and fees and costs remove roughly half the gross Sharpe.
E3-C15.evidence: R² 0.36–0.64; simulated gross Sharpe 1.8 → ≈ 1.0 after 2/20 (≈ 6%/yr) and 1–4%/yr costs; index net Sharpe 0.27–0.88 (1985–2012); implied weights 1m 24%, 3m 54%, 12m 22%.

P1-C08.evidence: Explains 71-94% of cross-sectional variance of test-portfolio expected returns; GRS rejects; fails on small, high-investment, low-profit stocks. US from 1963. IS.
P1-C08.implication: BUILD (risk model): FF5+UMD daily attribution for US cards.

P1-C09.claim: In the q-factor model, investment and ROE carry the strongest premia and absorb many anomalies.
P1-C09.evidence: US 1972-2011: investment 0.44%/month (t = 4.73), ROE 0.60% (t = 4.85), size 0.31% (t = 2.09); earnings-surprise alpha 0.14% (t = 0.92) vs Carhart 0.32% (t = 2.43). IS, gross.
P1-C09.implication: CONTEXT / alternative risk model; use quarterly ROE in signal design.

P1-C10.claim: The best-ranked factor model uses timely factors: {Mkt, SMB, IA, ROE, HMLm, UMD}.
P1-C10.evidence: US 1972-2013 Bayesian comparison: highest posterior; HMLm takes 99.5% of value-factor probability, ROE 99.5% of profitability probability.
P1-C10.implication: BUILD-candidate design: monthly-updated value and quarterly ROE; UMD in the risk model.

P1-C11.claim: Mispricing and behavioral factor models price anomalies better than FF5.
P1-C11.evidence: SY 1967-2013: average absolute alpha 0.18% vs 0.45% (FF5) vs 0.34% (q). DHS 1972-2014: 3 of 34 alphas significant vs 18 (FF5), 6 (q), 7 (SY); PEAD monthly Sharpe 0.35 (about 1.2 annualized). IS, gross.
P1-C11.implication: CONTEXT: supports an earnings-drift card (other panel); a PEAD factor is an optional attribution add-on.

P1-C12.claim: Most of the factor zoo is false at the single-signal level, and new factors need t > 3.
P1-C12.evidence: 316 factors; 27-53% of 296 significant factors are false discoveries (BHY 5% to Bonferroni); thresholds 3.39-3.78 by 2012, about 4.0 by 2032.
P1-C12.implication: Gate already consistent; require in-sample t ≥ 3 before a new characteristic becomes a card.

P1-C13.claim: With NYSE breakpoints and value weights, 64-85% of anomalies fail; liquidity anomalies almost all fail; micro-caps drive many results.
P1-C13.evidence: 447 anomalies: 64% insignificant at 5%, 85% at t = 3; 93% of liquidity anomalies fail. Micro-caps: 60.7% of firms, 3.21% of market cap (US 1967-2016).
P1-C13.implication: BUILD rule: capped VW weights and micro-cap exclusion in all KRX and US cards.

P1-C14.claim: Major factor themes replicate globally, with about one-third smaller out-of-sample alpha.
P1-C14.evidence: 153 factors, 93 countries: US replication 84.9% (OLS) / 77.3% (BY); OOS alpha 0.31% vs IS 0.45%/month; regional-only replication 60.7% (developed ex-US), 56.3% (EM). Chen-Zimmermann: 98% of 161 clear predictors reproduce (slope 0.90).
P1-C14.implication: CONTEXT: themes are real but smaller; use JKP Korea data for cross-checks (non-commercial licence).

P1-C15.claim: US anomaly returns decay sharply after publication, while outside the US the decay is not reliably observed.
P1-C15.evidence: McLean-Pontiff: 26% lower OOS, 58% lower post-publication (US). Jacobs-Müller: 241 anomalies in 39 markets, only the US declines reliably. Ilmanen: about 30% OOS drop over a century.
P1-C15.implication: Keep the 60% live haircut (US-calibrated, conservative for Korea); plan with 33-60%.

P1-C16.claim: Net of realistic costs and data-mining, the average anomaly earns about zero today, and only low-turnover strategies survive.
P1-C16.evidence: 204 anomalies: 68 bps/month gross IS falls to about 4 bps net after 2005 and publication; best at most about 10 bps. Strategies under 50% one-sided monthly turnover survive (NMV); short-term reversal fails at scale (FIM, 19 markets, 1998-2011).
P1-C16.implication: DROP high-turnover anomalies; quarterly or annual rebalancing with buy/hold buffers only.

P1-C17.claim: Profitability and investment premia are absent in pre-1963 data, whereas value survives.
P1-C17.evidence: US 1926-1963: value 0.43%/month (t = 2.09); profitability 0.09% (t = 0.86); investment 0.02% (t = 0.14); 8 of 36 accounting anomalies significant. True OOS.
P1-C17.implication: Downweight quality from 3 to 2; drop the "most consistent factor" claim.

P1-C18.claim: Value's 2007-2020 drawdown was the deepest since 1963 and came from revaluation, not broken fundamentals.
P1-C18.evidence: HML -55% over 13.5 years; revaluation -7.2 pp/yr; structural return +1.1%/yr (5.9% before 2007); value spread at the cheapest percentile in 2020; intangibles-adjusted HML drawdown -43%. US.
P1-C18.implication: CONTEXT: value cards need evaluation windows of 15+ years; decade-long droughts are normal.

P1-C19.claim: Value rebounded in 2021-22 and again in 2025-26, most strongly outside the US and in cheap technology.
P1-C19.evidence: World Value active: +0.4 (2021), +11.9 (2022), -12.0 (2023), -6.9 (2024), 0.0 (2025), +3.3 pp (12 months to Aug 2026). Europe +4.2 pp/yr (2021-25), Japan +3.1 pp/yr (2020-25). HML +13.55% over 12 months to Aug 2026. VLUE +80% over 1 year with 43% IT.
P1-C19.implication: BUILD-candidate for Korea and Japan value; US value only as a composite leg; always report sector composition.

P1-C20.claim: Stock momentum earns a positive premium but crashes in market rebounds after bear markets.
P1-C20.evidence: US 1927-2013 WML: 17.9%/yr, 30% volatility, Sharpe 0.60, monthly skew -4.70. July-August 1932 losers +232% vs winners +32%; March-May 2009 losers +163% vs winners +8%; 14 of 15 worst months followed negative 2-year market returns.
P1-C20.implication: CONTEXT: supports volatility scaling and the bear-state gate (already decided).

P1-C21.claim: US momentum indexes have earned roughly nothing over the cap-weighted market since 2012, before costs.
P1-C21.implication: BACKLOG: no standalone US stock-momentum card at 50 bp per side.

P1-C22.claim: Quality/profitability was the most consistent live factor in 2012-2025 but crashed in the 2025-26 junk rally.
P1-C22.evidence: World Quality +1.68 pp/yr (ahead 9 of 14 years, IR 0.43); USA Quality live +1.31 pp/yr (2013-25). RMW -16.44% over 12 months to Aug 2026; Small Weak +43.3% vs Small Robust +19.2%.
P1-C22.implication: BUILD-candidate as a composite leg; weight 2.

P1-C23.claim: Size is not a standalone premium in recent data or in Korea, and survives only after controlling for junk.
P1-C23.evidence: Korea 2002-15 SMB 0.16%/month (t = 0.45); R2000 minus R1000 -7.5 pp/yr (2021-25); SMB (FF3) -0.22% over 12 months to Aug 2026; size robust after quality control in 24 markets.
P1-C23.implication: DROP size as a signal; keep SMB in risk models.

P1-C24.claim: Value and momentum are negatively correlated in every market, so combinations beat either alone (Japan momentum is the weak case).
P1-C24.evidence: 1972-2011 combination Sharpe: US 0.63, UK 0.77, Europe 0.87, Japan 0.78, global 1.04; correlations -0.43 to -0.60; Japan momentum alone 0.09. Gross, IS.
P1-C24.implication: Build composite cards, not single-factor cards; Japan momentum weight 0.

P1-C25.claim: Factor premia exist internationally, but local factor models explain local returns better than global ones.
P1-C25.evidence: Value in all four developed regions; momentum everywhere except Japan; integrated pricing not supported. 18 EMs (1990-2011): value everywhere, momentum except Eastern Europe; local factors much better.
P1-C25.implication: Per-market risk models (local Korean factors) and per-market weights.

P1-C26.claim: In Korea, value, investment and quarterly profitability were priced in 2002-2015, while 2000-2019 replication favours value and (KOSDAQ-driven) momentum, not profitability.
P1-C26.evidence: Kang: HML 1.05%/month (t = 3.41), RMWq 0.65% (t = 2.75), CMA 0.66% (t = 3.57). Han-Lee-Kang: 37.8% of 148 anomalies VW-significant; value 69%, momentum 67% (20% excluding KOSDAQ), profitability 5%. IS, gross.
P1-C26.implication: BUILD-candidate: Korean value + quarterly ROE composite (DC-3); momentum DROP.

P1-C27.claim: Korea's cap-weighted benchmark is dominated by two semiconductor stocks, and that dominates any factor test.
P1-C27.evidence: MSCI Korea (Aug 2026): Samsung Electronics 34.55%, SK hynix 26.27%, IT 68.99%; 2025 +100.76%; 12 months +170.65%. AMRO: those two drove about half of the 2025 KOSPI market-cap gain; KOSPI P/B 0.99; over 60% of firms have ROE below 7%.
P1-C27.implication: Evaluate Korean cards against both cap-weighted and capped benchmarks; add a SEMI factor to attribution (DC-8).

P1-C28.claim: Anomaly returns concentrate on news days, pointing to mispricing, but factor-model tests alone cannot separate risk from mispricing.
P1-C28.evidence: 97 anomalies: returns 6x higher on earnings days and 50% higher on news days. KNS: reduced-form tests cannot discriminate. SY: short-leg sentiment slopes 2-3x larger. Ilmanen: little relation to macro risk.
P1-C28.implication: CONTEXT: treat premia as decaying mispricing (haircuts); long-only captures less than the published spread.

P1-C29.claim: QUANTGEN's gate is structurally underpowered for factor-tilt cards with net Sharpe or IR of 0.2-0.4.
P1-C29.evidence: P1 calc (Lo i.i.d. SE): 18 OOS years needed for SR 0.4 and 31 for SR 0.3. With about 27 OOS years: P(step 2) = 0.64 at SR 0.4; P(step 5) = 0.51 at IR 0.25 (0.31 with 10 years).
P1-C29.implication: Expect REVISE or INSUFFICIENT DATA; do not loosen the gate; pool markets and use the longest PIT histories.

P1-C30.claim: Every card needs a factor-attribution block, and cards with beta ≠ 1 need a beta-matched (Jensen's alpha) benchmark test.
P1-C30.evidence: Sharpe comparisons ignore cash mixing, while a Jensen's-alpha t-test asks whether adding the card raises the benchmark's Sharpe. Factor exposures plus expenses explain apparent fund skill (Carhart); passive tilts show CAPM alpha (FF 2004).
P1-C30.implication: BUILD: risk/attribution module (beta, CAPM alpha, FF5+UMD or local Korean alpha, Newey-West) on all cards; gate change only via pre-registration (DC-6).

P2-C01.claim: Classic single-index MA/filter/breakout/OBV rules lose significance once the full rule universe is counted and the sample moves past 1986.
P2-C01.evidence: DJIA 1897-1986 best rules RC p 0.000 (IS, gross); 1987-1996 OOS best 14.41%/yr, Sharpe 0.87, nominal p 0.004 → RC p 0.341; S&P futures 1984-1996 nominal 0.042 → RC 0.908; break-even 0.27%/trade
P2-C01.implication: DROP: no index MA/TRB alpha card

P2-C02.claim: Controlling false discoveries, even early-sample rule profits are wiped out by low costs and best rules cannot be picked ex ante.
P2-C02.evidence: DJIA 1897-2011, FDR portfolios: in-sample edge offset by low transaction costs; persistence tests fail
P2-C02.implication: DROP; adopt FDR + persistence in the family gate

P2-C03.claim: The literature's positive results cluster in pre-1990 samples and in methodologically weak studies.
P2-C03.evidence: 95 studies (1988-2004): 56 positive / 20 negative / 19 mixed; profits in US stocks until late 1980s, FX until early 1990s, futures until mid-1980s; break-even 0.39%/transaction for BLL rules on dividend-adjusted DJIA

P2-C04.claim: Across 49 markets in 2001-2007, no market (Korea included) has a significant rule after data-snooping adjustment.
P2-C04.evidence: 5,806 rules; Korea nominal p 0.298 → adjusted 0.942; Taiwan 0.076 → 0.748; gross
P2-C04.implication: DROP index rule-mining on KOSPI/KOSDAQ indices

P2-C05.claim: Where rules worked, it was in young, small or illiquid segments, and the edge faded with maturity and ETFs.
P2-C05.evidence: NASDAQ/Russell 2000 1990-2000 IS best 38.19%/47.10%/yr after 0.05% one-way (DJIA/S&P insignificant); stepwise SPA: edge weakens after ETF listings; tech/small caps significant 1995-2002, futile 2003-2010
P2-C05.implication: BACKLOG: KOSDAQ-segment families only, via the family gate; expect decay

P2-C06.claim: Rule profits in DJIA stocks were episodic and depended on short selling.
P2-C06.evidence: DJIA members 1928-2012: profits mainly mid-1960s to mid-1980s, reliant on shorts
P2-C06.implication: CONTEXT: a long-only read-only desk cannot harvest short-side profits

P2-C07.claim: Monthly technical indicators forecast the US equity premium out-of-sample and complement macro predictors.
P2-C07.evidence: S&P 500 OOS 1966-2011: R²OS 0.09-0.75% (14 indicators), PC-TECH 0.65%, PC-ALL 1.79%; CER gains 0.73-3.17%/yr (γ = 5), 0.40-2.82% after 50 bp; technicals catch declines near cycle peaks
P2-C07.implication: BACKLOG: risk-sizing input inside the macro overlay's [0.5, 1.0] band, never direction (consistent with the macro decision)

P2-C08.claim: Index MA timing mainly cuts drawdowns; return gains are inflated by look-ahead/data-mining bias and by averaged prices.
P2-C08.evidence: Faber S&P 500 1901-2012: 10.18% vs 9.32% CAGR, max DD 42.2% vs 83.7% (practitioner, mostly IS); Zakamulin: bias-corrected MA ≈ buy-and-hold, OOS with costs overstated; desk check: Shiller monthly-average returns lag-1 autocorrelation 0.274 vs SPY month-end 0.057; SMA10 1881-2023 9.35% (next month) vs 7.58% (skip month) vs buy-and-hold 9.16%
P2-C08.implication: DROP as alpha card (E1 already REJECT); allow display-only drawdown context; data lab must use month-end prices

P2-C09.claim: Diversified time-series momentum earned large gross alphas in 1965-2009 futures and across 1880-2016.
P2-C09.evidence: 58 futures 1985-2009: alpha 1.58%/month (t 7.99), Sharpe > 1, gross, no costs; 67 markets 1880-2016: 18.0% gross, 11.0% net of costs, 7.3% net of 2/20, Sharpe 0.76; trend t ≈ 10 since 1800
P2-C09.implication: CONTEXT: B3 already REJECT; reset expectations

P2-C10.claim: Trend following's excess return collapsed toward zero after 2009.
P2-C10.evidence: Excess return 6.3%/yr (2000-09) → 0.4% (2010-18), net of costs; net-of-fee decades 8.3% / 6.3% / 3.3% (1990s / 2000s / 2010-16); short trends withered; QUANTGEN B3 OOS Sharpe 0.08
P2-C10.implication: DROP futures TSMOM card; cut the prior "~1.0 diversified" expectation to 0.0-0.3 before haircut

P2-C11.claim: TSMOM's statistical evidence is weak once small-sample bias and volatility scaling are handled.
P2-C11.evidence: 55 assets 1985-2015: pooled t 4.34 < bootstrap critical 4.83 / 12.53; 8 of 55 significant; 3 with significant R²OS; TSM − TSH 0.14% (p 0.19); unscaled t 1.68; unscaled TSMOM ≈ buy-and-hold
P2-C11.implication: Gate design: benchmark trend against vol-scaled buy-and-hold and the TSH sign rule

P2-C12.claim: Volatility-scaled crypto trend has independent academic support and is QUANTGEN's strongest technical card.
P2-C12.evidence: Strong crypto TSMOM and attention effects; P/MA ratios predict daily bitcoin returns IS and OOS; MA rules best on high-frequency bitcoin; QUANTGEN C3 KRW-BTC OOS 1.22 [0.62, 1.77] vs 0.79, p 0.04, 1.17 at 2x costs
P2-C12.implication: BUILD (keep C3); use P/MA-ratio neighbours in the plateau test; apply the 60% haircut

P2-C13.claim: Proximity to the 52-week high predicts US returns better than past returns and does not reverse, but international profits rarely survive costs.
P2-C13.evidence: US 1963-2001 (6,6): 0.45%/month all months, 1.23% ex-January (t 7.06), risk-adjusted 1.13% (t 11.35), IS gross; 20 markets: profitable in 18, significant in 10, mostly insignificant after costs

P2-C14.claim: On KRX top-500 stocks the 52-week-high tilt is gross-positive in every decade but not significant net of 35 bp per side.
P2-C14.evidence: 1996-2026 monthly: L/S 0.66%/month gross (t 1.67), 0.25% net 35 (t 0.65); long-only vs universe 0.31% → 0.07%; 6-monthly rebalance L/S 5.73%/yr net 35 (gross t 1.37), long-only 1.34%/yr net 35
P2-C14.implication: BACKLOG card (long-only, 6-month rebalance); feature weight KRX 1, US 2

P2-C15.claim: Neutralizing 52-week-high distance inside momentum removes most of momentum's crash risk.
P2-C15.evidence: US 1930-2022: WML* 1.37%/month vs WML 1.19%; Sharpe 0.276 vs 0.159 (monthly); skew +0.13 vs −1.89; max DD −23.7% vs −74.1%
P2-C15.implication: BUILD-candidate construction rule for any momentum sleeve; test on KRX incl. 2026-07

P2-C16.claim: MA-based cross-sectional trend signals have US support but are weak in KRX.
P2-C16.evidence: US: trend factor Sharpe > 2x STR/MOM/LTR, 2009 +0.75%/month vs MOM −3.88%; MAD VW alpha ~9%/yr after institutional costs; KRX desk check: MA21/MA200 L/S 0.51%/month gross (t 1.28), 0.15% net 35; P/SMA200 0.28% (t 0.69), −0.12% net 35

P2-C17.claim: MA timing of high-volatility portfolios (HYZ) is large gross but lag- and cost-fragile in KRX.
P2-C17.evidence: US 1963-2009: MAP 5.17% → 18.55%/yr, alpha up to 21.38%, 15.8-18.0% after 25 bp; KRX 1996-2026 decile 10: 30.0%/yr gross (t 7.0), 18.0% net 35, 5.9% net 70; with one-day lag 18.0% gross, −6.0% net 70; 2016-26 with lag 6.7% gross (t 0.99)
P2-C17.implication: DROP stock-level card; optional BACKLOG ETF variant (e.g., a KOSDAQ 150 tracker at 3 bp)

P2-C18.claim: Short-term reversal is real gross but is a liquidity-provision return that retail costs cannot harvest.
P2-C18.evidence: US 1934-1987 decile spread 2.49%/month gross; weekly reversals (Lehmann); profits below likely costs (ACG); 30-50 bp/week net only in large caps with turnover control; VIX-predictable; tapered after 2011

P2-C19.claim: On KRX top-500 stocks, the weekly 5-day reversal, with or without the prior design's volume filter, is deeply negative net of 35 bp per side and has decayed gross.
P2-C19.evidence: 1996-2026 unconditional L/S 0.53%/week gross (t 6.47), decades 0.85 / 0.53 / 0.21; net 35 −0.59%/week (2016-26 −0.89); volume filter (> 1.5x): 0.44%/week gross, 2016-26 −0.10%, net 35 −0.88%/week; Σ
P2-C19.implication: DROP card; conflicts with the prior Korea ST-reversal weight 3 and the macro note's −2.95%/month (likely all-cap, gross)

P2-C20.claim: Volume's predictive sign depends on horizon and market; in KRX, high turnover predicts reversal, not short-term momentum.
P2-C20.evidence: US 1963-2018 VW: high-turnover winners continue +1.37%/month (t 4.74), 1.00% net; 22 developed markets +1.39%/month; weekly: high-transaction stocks reverse (CHN), falling-volume stocks reverse more (Cooper); KRX desk check 1996-2026: high-turnover WML −1.10%/month (t −2.24) gross
P2-C20.implication: DROP short-term momentum for KRX; volume only as a conditioning feature inside a pre-registered family

P2-C21.claim: Chart patterns carry statistical information but have no demonstrated net trading profit.
P2-C21.evidence: NYSE/AMEX and Nasdaq stocks 1962-1996 (350 sampled): 7 of 10 / 10 of 10 patterns change conditional return distributions; no cost or profit test

P2-C22.claim: A CNN reading chart images produces strong gross OOS sorts that concentrate in small caps and high turnover; there is no net-of-cost evidence.
P2-C22.evidence: US OOS 2001-2019: EW 1-month Sharpe 2.16-2.35 vs MOM 0.25, STR 0.55, WSTR 1.23; VW 0.45-0.49; turnover 155-187%/month; transfer to 26 markets Sharpe 0.7
P2-C22.implication: BACKLOG (research only); expect the same KRX cost failure as reversal

P2-C23.claim: Candlestick patterns do not predict returns in large US stocks; the one positive (Taiwan) is single-market.
P2-C23.evidence: 28 patterns on 35 DJIA stocks 1992-2002, EGARCH-null bootstrap: no predictability; Taiwan Top-50 2002-2008: three bullish reversal patterns profitable (costs unstated in abstract)

P2-C24.claim: Fibonacci retracements have no special support/resistance effect, and Elliott waves lack peer-reviewed tests.
P2-C24.evidence: DJ30, DAX30, NASDAQ-100 stocks 1968-2019: bounce probability at Fibonacci zones = non-Fibonacci zones; the rule trails buy-and-hold after risk; Elliott: only subjective, non-refereed work found

P2-C25.claim: Published RSI/MACD tests show market-specific, non-robust effects without snooping control, and a 52-rule oscillator family on SPY fails the Reality Check.
P2-C25.evidence: 5 OECD indices 1976-2002: significant only in Italy and Canada, 1% round trip; ASX 1996-2014: MACD insignificant, RSI small, no costs; desk check SPY 1999-2021 at 5 bp: 5 of 52 beat buy-and-hold Sharpe; best nominal p 0.18 → RC p 0.92; 0 of 52 beat it in 2010-2021
P2-C25.implication: DO-NOT-BUILD standalone oscillator cards; RSI/%B only as normalized reversal features

P2-C26.claim: Support/resistance levels and order clustering create small, real order-flow effects intraday.
P2-C26.evidence: FX intraday 1996-1998: bounce 60.8% at published levels vs 56.2% at arbitrary levels (+4.6 points; 13 of 16 significant); take-profits cluster at round numbers, stops just beyond
P2-C26.implication: BACKLOG intraday research (round-number features on KIS quotes); no daily card

P2-C27.claim: Technical-rule profitability rises and decays as the Adaptive Markets Hypothesis predicts: genuine early profits, decay after publication, slower decay for complex rules.
P2-C27.evidence: FX: Levich-Thomas portfolio 5.74% → −0.11%/yr, Sharpe 0.90 → −0.02 (1991-2005, net); breaks 1989-1993; simple FX rules ~8%/yr 1975-1990 → ~0 by the 1990s; conflicting: >21,000 rules on 30 currencies over 45 years still predictive under a stepwise test; anomaly returns halved after decimalization
P2-C27.implication: CONTEXT: rolling live-decay monitoring; V3 FX momentum REJECT stands; DROP FX technical cards

P2-C28.claim: With 100 trend rules on one index, the "best" rule's edge is a selection artifact.
P2-C28.evidence: SPY 1998-12-31 to 2021-03-31, SMA/TSMOM n = 5…250, 5 bp: best Sharpe 0.52 vs 0.37 (nominal p 0.17) → RC p 0.70; 0 of 100 beat buy-and-hold mean; IS winner +0.40 → OOS −0.22; 0 of 100 beat it in 2010-21; at 50 bp 0 of 100 beat it
P2-C28.implication: Family-level SPA/RC + FDR on top of the gate; DSR trials = family size

P2-C29.claim: KRX index-level trend timing added value only in 1997-2005 and failed in the 2024-2026 episodes.
P2-C29.implication: DROP KRX index trend card; display-only

P2-C30.claim: KRX 12-1 price momentum is weak, and its worst month was July 2026.
P2-C30.evidence: Top-500 EW 1996-2026: L/S 0.62%/month gross (t 1.82), 0.28% net 35 (t 0.83); 2026-07: winners (median past return +200%) −26.8% vs losers −1.9%, WML −27.2%; aggregate KOSPI market cap −21.4% in the month (marcap)
P2-C30.implication: CONTEXT: no KRX momentum card without nearhigh-neutral construction and volatility/concentration caps; test whether the bear gate would have fired

P2-C31.claim: Behavioural mechanisms (anchoring, disposition effect, slow diffusion) explain why a few price-state variables work, and disposition subsumes momentum.
P2-C31.evidence: Capital-gains overhang removes the predictive power of past returns (US cross-section); anchoring explains 52-week-high continuation without reversal; newswatcher/momentum-trader model; 692 fund managers mostly use technical analysis at horizons of weeks
P2-C31.implication: BACKLOG feature: capital-gains overhang from KRX OHLCV (data-check DC-I)

P3-C01.claim: The US value premium is small and statistically fragile among large stocks after 1991 and falls with firm size.
P3-C01.evidence: Market value 0.42%/mo (t 3.25) 1963-91 vs 0.11% (t 0.60) 1991-2019; big value 0.36 → 0.05; difference t 1.39; US, gross, IS→later sample
P3-C01.implication: CONTEXT: no standalone US value card

P3-C02.claim: The 2007-2020 value drawdown came mainly from valuation compression, not structural decay.
P3-C02.evidence: HML −54.8% (Jan-07 to Jun-20, 13.5 yrs); revaluation −7.2 pp/yr; structural +1.1 vs +5.9 pp/yr; 116% of shortfall; bootstrap p 2.3%; US, gross
P3-C02.implication: CONTEXT; do not time value by spread

P3-C03.claim: Including intangibles in book value materially improves value.
P3-C03.evidence: HML_INT 5.60%/yr SR 0.86 vs HML 3.49% SR 0.35 (1975-2018); alpha 3.86%/yr; 2007-18 +0.76% vs −2.77%; iHML drawdown −43.0% over 3.5 yrs; US, gross, IS
P3-C03.implication: BUILD feature: capitalised R&D in US-VQ book (counted as a trial)

P3-C04.claim: Timely prices in B/M add value alpha.
P3-C04.implication: BUILD rule: lagged filed book / current market cap

P3-C05.claim: US value since 2021 trailed growth cumulatively, and results depend heavily on construction.
P3-C05.evidence: IWD +96.8% vs IWF +112.8% (Jan-21 to Sep-26); VLUE +32.65% vs IWD +15.71% (2025); IWF P/B 15.74 vs IWD 3.27 (30 Sep 26); long-only, net of fees

P3-C06.claim: Gross profitability is a strong signal that hedges value.

P3-C08.claim: Buffett's record is largely explained by cheap, safe, quality stocks plus about 1.6× leverage.
P3-C08.evidence: SR 0.76; alpha insignificant after BAB + QMJ

P3-C09.claim: Profitability and investment effects are not universal; Japan is an exception, and HML is redundant in the US five-factor model.
P3-C09.evidence: Japan strong B/M, little profitability/investment relation; HML redundant given RMW/CMA
